job.organization: South Orange County Community College District

items.item_text: Attend trainings, meetings, workshops, and comply with mandatory certifications and diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives.
The following duties are typical for this classification. Incumbents may not perform all listed duties and may be required to perform additional or different duties to meet business needs.

Participates in the development, coordination, and support of the Surgical Technician academic program and related health and wellness instructional initiatives under the guidance of the Dean or designee.
Supports academic pathway development and student progression within the Surgical Technician program.
Conducts analyses related to program participants; tracks enrollment, persistence, completion, and outcomes using appropriate electronic systems.
Develops and maintains electronic calendars and tracking systems for student engagement, services, and academic progress monitoring.
Provides program information and guidance to students; refers complex academic or administrative issues to appropriate faculty or staff.
Assists with outreach activities, including informational sessions, recruitment events, advisory meetings, guest speakers, and program-related events.
Assists in planning, designing, and implementing academic support and program enhancement activities; participates in defining scope, timelines, and deliverables.
Coordinates instructional and student support resources for programs; assists in identifying short- and long-term academic needs and developing recommendations.
Participates in the development and implementation of program goals, objectives, policies, and academic priorities.
Researches policies, procedures, and promising practices; assists in developing and maintaining handbooks, forms, and related academic documentation.
Identifies operational or administrative challenges; conducts research, proposes alternative solutions, and assists with implementation.
Performs research, administrative, financial, and analytical duties in support of assigned academic projects and initiatives.
Creates and maintains publications and promotional materials, including newsletters, directories, flyers, catalogs, and handbooks.
Updates and maintains program websites and social media platforms related to the Surgical Technician and health and wellness academic programs.
Coordinates activities with internal staff and external partners, including local, state, and federal agencies, advisory partners, and community organizations.
Collaborates in building and sustaining a network of community-based organizations that support student learning experiences and program enrichment.
Represents the program on committees, task forces, and advisory groups; prepares agendas, reports, presentations, and supporting materials.
Serves as a point of contact for inquiries related to the program; participates in community outreach and educational activities.
Maintains program records; prepares reports and briefings related to program scope, timelines, progress, and resource use.
Assists in training and providing work direction to student workers and assigned staff.
Performs related duties as required.
Principles and practices of academic program administration, coordination, and evaluation.
Learn and apply college, district, and academic program policies and procedures.
Educational administration principles applicable to community college programs.
Coordinate services and activities for academic and student support programs.
Instructional programs and academic requirements related to surgical technology and allied health.
Use basic project coordination tools to support program implementation.
Basic project coordination and academic planning principles.
Collect, analyze, interpret, and report academic and program data from multiple sources.
Research methods, data tracking, and reporting related to student outcomes.
Build and maintain collaborative working relationships with students, faculty, staff, and community partners.
College administrative services, student services, and institutional operations.
Provide accurate academic program information and high-quality student support.
Federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including FERPA, ADA, and confidentiality requirements.
Work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.
Office practices, recordkeeping systems, and reporting tools.
Maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment and discretion.
Use of electronic systems, databases, and standard office software.
Provide training and work direction to student workers and temporary staff.
Effective student service practices and academic communication techniques.
Work occasional evenings or weekends as required.
Occupational hazards and standard safety practices.
Report to work on a regular and consistent basis, as scheduled, to the assigned job.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING ENVIRONMENT

The conditions herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.

Environment: Work is performed primarily in a standard office setting; frequent interaction with students, faculty, staff, and community partners; subject to interruptions and use of standard office equipment.

Physical: Requires sufficient mobility to sit or stand for extended periods; occasional bending, reaching, and lifting of light to moderate materials; repetitive hand movements for computer use; verbal and auditory communication; occasional travel to meetings or events.
Vision and hearing : within normal ranges with or without accommodation.
Diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and disability backgrounds of community college students.
Communicate clearly and effectively in written and oral English.
